page: Amazon Web Services i4i.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, providing 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration bundles 64.0 GB of DDR4 system memory clocked at 3 GHz, allocating 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside a dedicated 1875 GB local NVMe SSD. The processor features 54 MB of L3 cache and supports specialized instruction sets, including AVX-512 VNNI, AES-NI, and SHA-NI. Networking throughput offers a 5 Gbps baseline, and the server does not include discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results place the i4i.2xlarge in the middle performance tiers for standard computing and data processing. The instance scored 1,593.0 in single-core and 5,905.0 in multi-core Geekbench evaluations, aligned with a PassMark CPU score of 11,458.75. Memory performance is consistent, demonstrating cached read bandwidth of 413.76 GB/sec and uncached read rates of 55.85 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 8.49 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 12.29 GB/sec static web throughput. Tradeoffs appear in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, which scored in the bottom 25% at 31.32 GB/sec, while CPU-bound medium LLM inference achieved only 7.44 tokens per second on text generation.

The combination of a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory profile with direct-attached high-speed NVMe capacity yields strong qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense storage environments, avoiding network-attached storage latency and transfer costs. The instance is well suited for transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, in-memory caches, search indexes, and operational data pipelines requiring high disk and memory throughput.

Memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, matched with 1875 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage and a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system includes AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions while omitting GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, the server registers balanced mid-range compute scores, including a Geekbench multi-core mark of 5,905.0 and 8.49 million Redis SET operations per second, though multi-threaded decompression and AI inference show lower relative throughput. Thanks to its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high-speed local NVMe volume, i4i.2xlarge is well positioned for I/O-intensive workloads, including transactional databases, NoSQL datastores, distributed data caching, and real-time analytical processing.
